text: Harrow Creek Goods' three-lesson capstone pulled on every chapter of this course, not just the Kubernetes-objects chapter. This lesson traces each decision back to the chapter that actually made it possible, then closes the course and points to what's next.

Chapter 1's layer model and multi-stage builds needed no introduction when Lesson 29 containerized both services. Chapter 2 is why the runtime image went distroless, ran as non-root, and got a real version tag instead of latest. Chapter 3 is why both services became Deployments with ReplicaSets, not bare pods, and Chapter 4 is the Service model the Ingress in Lesson 30 routed traffic to without re-explaining it.

Chapter 5 is exactly what made order-worker's PersistentVolumeClaim possible -- dynamic provisioning from a StorageClass instead of a hand-created volume. Chapter 6 is why Lesson 30 ended as one Helm chart with a single values.yaml instead of four separate YAML files applied by hand, producing both a full release and a smaller one from the same source.

Chapter 7 is the lens Lesson 31's incident has to be read through: BestEffort QoS, the real difference between a container getting OOMKilled and a pod getting Evicted, and a LimitRange as the namespace-wide fix. Those ideas stopped being abstract the moment one missing resources block took down two healthy neighbors.

Across three lessons, Harrow Creek deployed a real two-service application, wrapped it in routing, storage, and a Helm chart, and worked through a resource-governance failure at both the pod level and the namespace level. That's the real job: not just getting a Deployment to reach Running, but understanding every object around it well enough to explain why a neighbor's mistake became everyone's incident.

Docker, Kubernetes & Container Platforms is now complete: eight chapters covering fundamentals, production images, core objects, networking, storage, Helm, and security, proven on one real application including a recovered incident. The Advanced Specialization stage continues next with Cloud Reliability, Monitoring & FinOps.
